title: Invited Lecturer - Baffour W. Osei (Princeton Robotics Lab Manager)
description:
Student-led STEM clubs face a unique challenge: high enthusiasm, limited time, limited
budgets, and constant member turnover. When students are only around for one to two years, projects often stall, knowledge is lost, and expensive equipment goes underused. 

This session focuses on how to design, sustain, and scale technical projects when club membership is constantly in flux. Using examples from robotics, software, manufacturing, embedded systems, mechatronics, and more, the talk will explore practical strategies for building lightweight but effective systems including documentation, onboarding, project scoping, and maintenance practices that students will actually follow. Emphasis will be placed on structuring projects so that students with different interests (software, hardware, mechanical, integration, non-STEM, etc.) can meaningfully contribute without fragmenting the effort.

The session will also address how to create short learning pathways that lead to resume-worthy outcomes within one or two semesters. It will also discuss the power of onboarding modules and projects as an on-ramp into topics of interest. The goal is to help clubs keep the fire burning by turning projects into living systems that outlast individual members while remaining accessible, engaging, and educational.
